summary: Core relay-owned topology holds when ingress, relay, RPC adapter, approval gate, and OS isolation are explicit seams.
Standard RPC confirm carries no signed decision capability; canonical-input and final-handler approval controls are required.
Current Serve docs establish anti-spoofed identity headers, usable only as attested auth bootstrap; WSS propagation remains a runtime gate.
Replay/barrier/idempotency model is coherent but must be fault-tested; recovered dispatching remains indeterminate.
Redaction must precede sequenced persistence and cover snapshots, catalogs, cache, audit, fan-out, and push.
Session navigation requires isolated active-session children or exclusive idle switch_session semantics.
Documentation narrows iOS/Android and WCAG gates, but real-device and assistive-technology validation remains open.
Approval TOCTOU or post-gate input mutation.
Unverified relay crash and snapshot-barrier behavior.
Deployment identity, backend-bypass, authorization, and OS-containment gaps.
Raw-data leakage through a redaction-bypass path.
Unverified private-origin push and mobile stale-approval races.
Pinned dependency behavior can drift on upgrade.

limitations: does not validate real Pi scheduling, relay database atomicity, Serve WSS, mobile devices, or assistive technology
